papers.title: Adaptive Relational Learning on Multi-instance Quantum Data with Photonic Processors
papers.findings: SectionII/Eqs1-7 learns independent local transformations then measures an n-state Bargmann invariant with CYCLE/SWAP. Pairwise transition probabilities and higher-order geometric phases are explicit existing learning features. SectionIII/p4 distinguishes its Gaussian mechanism examples from quantum advantage over efficient Gaussian-specific methods.
papers.limits: Selected setup, abstract and p4 task passages only; full proofs, later shot-complexity comparison, implementation blueprint, experiments and code not audited. The source uses multiple quantum-data inputs and collective measurement, not the native classical-token/40-effect head. Neither its higher-order label construction nor shot advantage transfers automatically.

papers.title: Quantum tangent kernel
papers.findings: SectionII-B/Eq8 and SectionIII/Eq17 define tangent kernels from inner products of parameter derivatives. Using the initialization kernel to model training is conditional on a valid local linearization/lazy regime. The reported illustration uses a ten-qubit model, MSE and SGD; no general native AdamW guarantee follows.
papers.limits: Title/abstract and pp3-4 selected setup read. Full experiments, appendices/code and asymptotic theory not reproduced. An instantaneous derivative inner product remains a known tool even outside a verified global lazy approximation; it is not novel theory or a forecast of native alignment gain.

papers.title: Complex Dynamics in Simple Neural Networks: Understanding Gradient Flow in Phase Retrieval
papers.findings: Section1/p2 Eqs1-4 specify real Gaussian sensing directions, teacher-generated squared projections, a quartic intensity loss and spherical gradient flow. p9 explains reliance on a symmetry-supported random-guess phase and leaves broader learning settings open.
papers.limits: Selected abstract/setup/limitations only; full statistical-physics derivation, thresholds, simulations and proofs not audited. Complex Dynamics in the title refers to dynamics, not complex-amplitude training data. NLP contextual features, normalized attention, CE and AdamW do not satisfy the specified model merely because Born scores are squared overlaps.

papers.title: L2 Regularization versus Batch and Weight Normalization
papers.findings: Sections2-3 show normalization can preserve a function while rescaling parameter gradients; Section5.3/Table1 explicitly discuss Adam retaining scale dependence. This is direct prior for a normalization/optimizer explanation, not a new quantum mechanism.
papers.limits: Selected pp1-5 read, not complete experiments or code. The paper discusses L2/normalization and Adam; the present clipped AdamW first-step bound is separately scoped. No transfer of equilibrium weight-scale approximations or every displayed formula was assumed. NIPS2017 footer observed, publisher record not separately certified.
